name: Cabo Delgado insurgency (Islamic State Mozambique), Mozambique
started: 2017-10-05 (Mocimboa da Praia attack; IS Mozambique Province split from ISCAP in May 2022)
summary: Islamic State's Mozambique branch keeps a stubborn insurgency alive in Cabo Delgado's coastal districts, mixing abductions for ransom, ambushes on the N380 highway and long-range raids into Niassa, while Rwandan and Mozambican forces guard towns and the LNG zone. Militant-linked deaths rose 51% to 531 in 2025 (Africa Center), and attacks on civilians climbed from 9 in July to 19 in September 2026 (ACLED). It matters because TotalEnergies restarted its giant LNG project at Afungi in January 2026, after a five-year suspension caused by the 2021 Battle of Palma.

sides.name: Mozambique and partners
members: Mozambique Defence Armed Forces (FADM), incl. navy; Northern Operation Theater HQ moved to Mocimboa da Praia in July 2026
Local Force militia (under military command since 2023)
Tanzanian troops in Nangade border area
backers: European Union, Rwanda and Algeria (training of FADM units)
TotalEnergies (LNG project whose security underpins a long-term international presence)
sides.strength: No figures for RDF or FADM in the sources retrieved.

sides.name: Islamic State Mozambique (ISM)
sides.strength: No overall figure; a Niassa raiding force numbered up to 150 fighters in July 2026 (ACLED).

background: The insurgency began in October 2017 in Mocimboa da Praia, and peaked with the 2021 capture of Palma, which froze TotalEnergies' LNG project. Rwanda's July 2021 intervention and a southern African mission (SAMIM, since withdrawn) retook the main towns, but ISM adapted into small mobile groups based in forests like Catupa and coastal areas such as Quiterajo.

Why it matters: the LNG project is one of Africa's largest energy investments, and ISM's survival despite years of Rwandan operations shows the limits of a town-guarding strategy. ISM also targets fishers and traders on the coast, while Mozambican forces have been accused of killing fishers at sea.
year: RDF forces killed at least 35 ISM fighters near Cogolo around 30 Nov 2025 and set up a post at Pangane; ISM killed five RDF soldiers at Cogolo on 24 Dec. TotalEnergies, having lifted force majeure in Oct 2025, restarted the LNG project on 27 Jan 2026. ISM overran two FADM positions in the Catupa forest on 31 Jan 2026 and held the forest through weeks of fighting (at least 15 killed on 23 Feb, including three Rwandan soldiers). On 15 Mar a FADM navy vessel fired on six fishing boats in Calugo bay, killing 13 fishers; commanders admitted responsibility. In July the military's northern headquarters moved to Mocimboa da Praia. An ISM force of up to 150 fighters crossed into Montepuez and Niassa from 27 July; FADM killed at least 16 at Shamba Kubwa on 1 Aug, and on 3 Sept ISM raided a hunting camp near Nanlixa, Marrupa, killing two staff and taking three hostages, released on 4 Oct for about US$53,000. Attacks on civilians, many involving abductions for ransom, rose to 19 in September across Macomia, Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe and Nangade; ISM claimed an IED on an RDF patrol on the Chinda-Mbau road on 16 Sept.
situation: As of late October 2026 ISM is active in the Macomia coast and Quiterajo, around Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe and Nangade, and has shown it can move south toward Ancuabe and west into Niassa. RDF and FADM conduct sporadic operations, including marine operations, from Mbau and Mocimboa da Praia; Tanzanian troops operate in Nangade. TotalEnergies is considering accelerating LNG expansion with about 10,000 workers on site. The US advised against all travel to Niassa in August 2026.
technical: ISM attacks on civilians in Macomia, Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe and Nangade: 9 (July), 11 (August), 19 (September 2026); 11 of September's involved abductions, with ransoms of 1,500 to 70,000 meticais (ACLED).

Niassa raid: up to 150 fighters reached Ntola (Montepuez) on 27 July 2026, fought FADM on 30 July, were hit at Shamba Kubwa on 1 Aug (16+ killed), split into small groups and moved toward Balama and Marrupa; about 30 entered Marrupa on 31 Aug (ACLED).
Hostage economy: three hunters' camp hostages released 4 Oct 2026 for about 3.2 million meticais (about US$53,000) (ACLED).
IED use: ISM IED on a Rwandan vehicle in Macomia (9 Jan 2026) and on an RDF patrol on the Chinda-Mbau road (16 Sept 2026).
Catupa forest near the N380 is a key ISM base: two FADM positions overrun on 31 Jan 2026; ambush on a commercial convoy near Quinto Congresso on 22 Feb (4 killed) (ACLED; Wikipedia).
Coastal raiding: abductions of fishers off Macomia and Mocimboa da Praia, incl. Tambuzi Island (Aug 2026); mortar fire on Pangane (Jan 2026).
Security-force abuses: FADM navy killed 13 fishers in Calugo bay (15 Mar 2026); at least 85 fishers killed in 10 incidents since Jan 2024 (ACLED).

Force posture: Northern Operation Theater HQ moved from Pemba to Mocimboa da Praia (July 2026); FADM blocks routes along the Lugenda river and R698; RDF guards the Mbau area and raids Quiterajo; Tanzanian troops killed two cross-border insurgents in Nangade (20 Sept 2026).
ISM logistics: supply networks inside Mocimboa da Praia (arrests over deliveries to Malinde, Aug 2026); possible support from Tanzania via Nangade (ACLED).
LNG: TotalEnergies lifted force majeure in Oct 2025, restarted on 27 Jan 2026, and was considering accelerated expansion with about 10,000 workers on site (30 Sept 2026).
casualties: Africa Center (2025 data): 531 militant Islamist-linked deaths in northern Mozambique, up 51%, of which 260 civilians. Incident data 2026: at least 15 killed at Catupa on 23 Feb (incl. 3 Rwandan soldiers); 13 fishers killed by the navy on 15 Mar; 16+ militants killed at Shamba Kubwa on 1 Aug; 2 camp staff killed on 3 Sept. No rolling 12-month figure found.
displaced: Over 700 people fled after attacks at Litandacua (N380) and Pangane in Aug-Sept 2026 (IOM via ACLED). No current provincial IDP total retrieved.

timeline.event: RDF kills at least 35 ISM fighters near Cogolo (approximate date).
ISM kills five RDF soldiers at Cogolo.
TotalEnergies restarts the Mozambique LNG project.
ISM overruns two FADM positions in the Catupa forest.
At least 15 killed in clashes in Catupa, including three Rwandan soldiers.
FADM navy kills 13 fishers in Calugo bay.
ISM force of up to 150 reaches Ntola, Montepuez, starting the Niassa incursion.
FADM kills 16+ ISM fighters at Shamba Kubwa.
ISM raids a hunting camp in Marrupa, Niassa; two staff killed, three hostages taken.
Niassa hostages released for about US$53,000.

outlook: Watch the rainy season (from about December), which usually reduces ISM mobility, whether ISM keeps expanding into Niassa and Nangade, the scale of abductions for ransom, Rwanda's commitment as Kigali faces pressure over DRC, and security around the accelerating LNG build-out.

battles.name: ISM incursion into Montepuez and Niassa
battles.place: Ntola and Shamba Kubwa (Montepuez, Cabo Delgado) to Marrupa (Niassa), Mozambique; mapped near Shamba Kubwa/Nairoto, approximate
battles.outcome: ISM force split into small groups after FADM attacks but raided a hunting camp and extracted a ransom.
battles.forces: ISM force of up to 150 fighters; FADM blocking forces on the Lugenda river and R698.
battles.losses: 16+ ISM killed at Shamba Kubwa (1 Aug); 2 hunting camp staff killed (3 Sept); 3 hostages freed for about US$53,000 (4 Oct).
battles.significance: ISM's first incursion into Niassa since May 2025 and evidence of a support network deep inland; led to a US 'do not travel' warning for Niassa.

battles.name: FADM navy shooting of fishers in Calugo bay
battles.place: Calugo bay near Mocimboa da Praia, Cabo Delgado, Mozambique (coordinates approximate)
battles.outcome: Commanders admitted responsibility at a public meeting on 25 Mar.
battles.losses: At least 13 fishers killed, 3 injured (ACLED; Wikipedia).
battles.significance: Part of a pattern of at least 85 fishers killed by security forces since Jan 2024, which feeds coastal grievances ISM exploits.

battles.name: Battles for the Catupa forest
battles.place: Catupa forest near the N380 and Quinto Congresso, Macomia/Muidumbe, Cabo Delgado, Mozambique (coordinates approximate)
sides: FADM, Rwanda Defence Force, police, Local Force
battles.outcome: ISM overran two FADM positions, retook the Catupa position (8 Feb) and still controls the forest.
battles.forces: ISM fighters; FADM positions; RDF and police reinforcements.
battles.losses: IS claimed 9 FADM killed (31 Jan); 5 FADM and 3 militants killed (8 Feb); 4 killed in convoy ambush incl. a child (22 Feb); at least 15 killed incl. 3 Rwandan soldiers (23 Feb).
battles.significance: Showed ISM can hold ground next to the main N380 highway as the LNG project restarted.
